rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / DATA AND LOOPS / CHAPTER 5

slides.title: Loops
slides.main: Write an action once, run it as many times as needed.

items.title: while
items.sub: While the condition is true, the body repeats

items.title: Exit and skip
items.sub: break ends the loop, continue ends one pass

body.text: Conditions gave the program forks, but every action still runs once. A loop removes that limit: processing a thousand emails with one piece of code is a real task, not a feat.

slides.title: The while loop
slides.main: While the condition is true, the loop body repeats again and again.

body.text:
n = 3
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n = n - 1
ON SCREEN
Same indentation as in conditions: the loop body is everything shifted right.

slides.title: Infinite loop
slides.sub: A condition that never becomes false
slides.main: Something in the body must change, so the condition can become false.

body.text:
n = 3
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    # the counter never changes: the loop is endless!

cells.title: A timeout saves you
cells.sub: The trainer stops code that exceeds the limit

slides.title: The for loop
slides.main: No counters, no bounds, no manual step: just the point of the task.

body.text:
for ch in "hello":
    print(ch)
ON SCREEN

h
e
l
l
o
On each pass, the variable ch gets the next character of the word.

slides.title: range
slides.main: The right bound of range is never included.

body.text:
for i in range(5):
    print(i)

cells.title: range(1, 6)
cells.sub: From one to five: six is left out

cells.title: range(0, 10, 2)
cells.sub: The third argument is the step: 0 2 4 6 8

slides.title: Accumulator
slides.sub: A piggy bank that grows on every pass
slides.main: Start value and action change: sums, counters and products.

body.text:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 101):
    total += i
print(total)

cells.title: total += i
cells.sub: +=: add and write back to the same variable

slides.title: break
slides.main: break saves passes and makes the intent clear: no need to go on.

body.text: ON SCREEN
First digit found: no need to check the rest of the string.

slides.title: continue
slides.sub: Skip the rest of the body, go to the next pass
slides.main: break closes the whole loop, continue only one pass.

body.text: Remainder of division by two is zero: the number is even, no printing.

slides.title: while True and break
slides.sub: An endless loop with an exit test inside
slides.main: An exit mid-body is more honest than a forced condition on top: the exit point is visible.

cells.title: while True
cells.sub: “Repeat forever”: how menus and surveys are built

slides.title: Nested loops
slides.sub: A loop inside a loop: the work multiplies
slides.main: For each pass of the outer loop, the inner one runs in full.

slides.title: String accumulator
slides.sub: Building a new string from the characters of the old one
slides.main: Strings are immutable: do not edit the old one, build a new one each time.

body.text:
word = "hello"
rev = ""
for ch in word:
    rev = ch + rev
print(rev)
olleh
Each letter is prepended to the result: the first ends up last.

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: for: when we know what we go over. while: when we go “until something happens”.

cells.title: range(1, 5)
cells.sub: The right bound is excluded: you need range(1, 6)

cells.title: The while counter
cells.sub: Forgot to change it: an endless loop

body.text: Off-by-one is the sneakiest: the code works but does one step fewer than you want.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Write an action once, run it as many times as needed.

items.title: while
items.sub: Repeats the body while the condition holds

items.title: for
items.sub: Goes over elements; range gives numbers

body.text: Loops need room: next chapter is lists, the central data type of Python. Hundreds of values in one variable, and one for goes over them all.
